why: The student says the file can be renamed to Greeting.java while it still contains public class hello, which treats the file name and class name as independent; that contradicts Java's rule that public class hello must be in hello.java, so javac would reject it.

concepts.quote: I can rename the file to Greeting.java and keep public class hello.
concepts.why: This applies the documented wrong rule that a public class can be saved under any file name.
This treats the class name as independent of the file name, which is the documented misconception for class declarations.

concepts.quote: I can rename the file to Greeting.java
